identification.summary: Wisteria Tsunami is Microsoft's name for a private sector offensive actor (PSOA) it lists as India-based; Microsoft's taxonomy places PSOAs in the Tsunami family, and lists DEV-0605 and MintedSoil as other names for it [S1]. A MISP galaxy entry and a breach database list the Indian firm CyberRoot as a synonym of DEV-0605/MintedSoil [S2][S3]. The mapping of Wisteria Tsunami to CyberRoot rests on these aggregator entries, not on a Microsoft report I could open.
identification.notes: Search snippets for the Microsoft naming page and the MISP galaxy page were garbled and one snippet appeared to show an Israel origin line adjacent to the DEV-0605 line; the origin 'India' is as stated in the search summary of Microsoft's naming list and MISP [S1][S2]. 'MintedSoil' is unrelated to Mint Sandstorm (an Iranian actor) in the sources reviewed; no source connected them. Malpedia reportedly lists Wisteria Tsunami alongside Storm-0252 and the alias CHATTY SPIDER, but the mapping was not confirmed [S1].

attribution.basis: Microsoft classifies the actor as a private sector offensive actor, a commercial entity category, rather than a state organ [S1]. Aggregators equate it with CyberRoot, an Indian firm [S2][S3]. US lawmakers (not an agency finding) asked on 2026-09-09 that Commerce add CyberRoot, BellTroX and Sunkissed Organic Farms to the Entity List, alleging 15+ years of espionage against US citizens, businesses and their lawyers; the firms deny wrongdoing [S5][S6][S7]. No government attribution of Wisteria Tsunami itself was found.

objectives: As a PSOA, the category Microsoft describes is one of commercial actors that sell cyber capabilities to customers [S1]. Reporting on CyberRoot describes hack-for-hire collection against individuals, including social engineering and phishing aimed at account access and data collection, per Meta [S4]. Customer identities and motives for specific tasking are not established in the reviewed sources.

sectors: Legal (law firms, lawyers, alleged by US lawmakers)
targeting.notes: Targeting statements are about CyberRoot as reported by Meta via press coverage [S4] and by US lawmakers [S5][S6][S7]. Lawmakers allege more than 1,000 attorneys at major US law firms were targeted [S7]. These are allegations; the firms deny wrongdoing [S7]. Country lists and the Myanmar/India/Taiwan/China figures sometimes quoted alongside the Meta report relate to a separate ~900-account China-based network in the same report, not CyberRoot, and were removed.

capabilities.summary: Meta removed over 40 Facebook and Instagram accounts it tied to CyberRoot Risk Advisory, and said the activity manifested primarily as social engineering and phishing rather than malware [S4]. No Microsoft technical report on Wisteria Tsunami or DEV-0605 tooling was found [S1].

campaigns.name: Meta takedown of CyberRoot-linked accounts
campaigns.summary: Meta removed more than 40 Facebook and Instagram accounts it attributed to CyberRoot Risk Advisory Private, used for social engineering and phishing against individuals such as executives, lawyers, activists and journalists [S4].

campaigns.name: US lawmakers request Entity List action
campaigns.summary: Sens. Wyden and Whitehouse and Rep. Harrigan asked Commerce to add BellTroX, CyberRoot and Sunkissed Organic Farms to the Entity List over alleged long-running hack-for-hire espionage; no Commerce action was identified as of 2026-09-11 in the coverage reviewed [S5][S6][S7].

diamond.adversary: Commercial hack-for-hire firm (Microsoft: PSOA, India); linked by aggregators to CyberRoot [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Social engineering and phishing for account access; malware not the primary mode per Meta [S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Fake social media accounts on Facebook and Instagram (over 40 removed) [S4].
diamond.victim: Lawyers, executives, activists, journalists and others across multiple countries [S4][S7].
diamond.socioPolitical: Commercial customers select targets under the PSOA model [S1]; US Congress members are pressing for sanctions-type controls [S5].

gaps: Microsoft's own publication describing Wisteria Tsunami/DEV-0605 activity was not found; WebFetch of learn.microsoft.com failed, so the naming page was seen only through search summaries.
Origin in the garbled search result of the naming page was ambiguous; verify directly.
The CyberRoot to Wisteria Tsunami mapping rests on MISP and a breach database; no vendor report establishing it was found.
Meta's primary report, the Wyden press release and TechCrunch article were not opened (fetch failed); details come from search summaries and secondary coverage.
Customers, malware, infrastructure indicators, first-observed date, and the Storm-0252/CHATTY SPIDER overlap are unverified.
Overlap with BellTroX/Dark Basin (Citizen Lab) is not established for CyberRoot in reviewed sources; keep clusters separate.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Operational environment: commercial hack-for-hire actors target individuals and professionals, notably lawyers and executives, by social engineering and phishing via social media accounts [S4][S7]. MLCOA (assessment): continued phishing and social-engineering of private persons on behalf of paying customers. MDCOA (assessment): targeting extended to defense-adjacent personnel or contractors (no sourced evidence of such targeting). Candidate indicators: fake professional-persona accounts approaching personnel on social platforms; phishing aimed at personal and legal-sector accounts. Evidence is thin; no technical IOCs were sourced.
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: track Microsoft, Meta and congressional/Commerce developments on these firms [S1][S4][S5]. Authorities: any response is a law enforcement, Commerce or State matter, not a military one on this evidence. Mission assurance: brief personnel and contractors on social-media-based phishing and personal account hygiene [S4]. Coordination: route observations to the cyber threat intelligence enterprise and defense industrial base partners; engagement of legal-sector partners is a possibility given reported targeting [S7].
